scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which is outside the standard 30-day window due to travel.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Javier Gonzalez and I'm 64. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?
Hi Javier. I see. Our policy is 30 days, so you're outside that window. I'm not sure what you expect me to do about that.
I understand it's past the window, but I was traveling and didn't have access to my account. Is there any exception for this?
I don't have any exceptions. Can you give me your account number so I can at least see what account you're talking about?

Okay, I see the account. You said you canceled 34 days ago? I'm just going to go ahead and put a request in for a refund, but I don't know if it will be approved. I'm escalating this to the billing department.
Wait, you're escalating it? Can't you just process the refund yourself? I've been a customer for a long time.
I don't have the authority to override the 30-day rule. It has to go to a specialist. They will contact you eventually.

escalation_reason: Agent claimed lack of authority to override standard policy and deferred the decision to a specialist department.
